log.ready: Ready. Nothing leaves this computer except SSH to your Kindle.
conn.title: Searching for your Kindle
conn.step1: Wake the Kindle and open KOReader
conn.scanning: Also searching this computer's local network, in case the Kindle got a new address. Only a host with your Kindle's host key is accepted.
conn.unreachable: No answer at this address. The Kindle may be asleep, off Wi-Fi, or at a new address.
conn.portClosed: This address answers, but nothing is listening on the SSH port: KOReader's SSH server is not running.
conn.hostKeyMismatch: The host at this address presents a different host key than your paired Kindle. ember will not connect to it and never accepts a new key on its own. If you did not reset KOReader, another device may be posing as your Kindle.
conn.authRejected: Your Kindle answered but refused ember's key. Check that ember's key is still in koreader/settings/SSH/authorized_keys.
conn.authRejectedPasswordless: Your Kindle answered but refused the passwordless login. Tick "Login without password (DANGEROUS)" again in Settings → Network → SSH server.
pair.title: Pair your Kindle
pair.intro: ember needs one thing from you: open KOReader's SSH server for a moment, with passwordless login on. It finds the Kindle, shows it to you, and installs its own key.
pair.step1: On the Kindle, open KOReader and connect to the same Wi-Fi as this computer.
pair.step4: Tap "SSH server" to start it, then search below.
pair.why: Passwordless login stays on only until ember's key is installed. You will switch it off at the end. Nothing is written to the Kindle before you confirm it.
pair.scanningBody: Looking for KOReader's SSH server on port 2222 in this computer's local subnets. This takes a few seconds.
pair.foundIntro: Pick your Kindle. Check that the KOReader version and the open book match what you see on it.
pair.noneFound: No Kindle answered. Check that KOReader's SSH server is running and that both devices are on the same Wi-Fi, or type its address below.
pair.noPasswordless: Passwordless login is off, so ember cannot read anything from this host yet. It can still pair if you copied ember's key over USB.
pair.installSurvey: Reading KOReader's settings and free space
pair.installKey: Adding ember's public key to authorized_keys
pair.installVerify: Logging in with the key only
pair.lockIntro: ember's key works. Now, on the Kindle, close the passwordless door:
pair.lock1: In KOReader: Settings → Network → SSH server → tap "SSH server" to stop it.
pair.lock3: Tap "SSH server" again to start it. ember reconnects with its key and this turns green.
pair.waitingLock: Waiting for passwordless login to be refused
pair.locked: Passwordless login is off. Only ember's key gets in.
pair.usbBody: Copy ember's public key to the Kindle over USB instead. ember then pairs with the key alone.
pair.usb1: Connect the Kindle by USB and open the koreader/settings/SSH folder (create SSH if missing).
pair.usb2: Add the line below to the file authorized_keys there (create it if missing; keep any lines already in it).
pair.usb3: Eject, start KOReader's SSH server with "Login with key only", then search.
err.hostKeyMismatch: This host's key is not the one you confirmed. ember will not connect to it. If you did not reset KOReader, someone else may be answering at that address.
err.keyNotAccepted: The Kindle refused both ember's key and a passwordless login. Turn on "Login without password" or copy the key over USB, then try again.
err.verifyFailed: The key was added but a key-only login still failed.
err.unknownDevice: That Kindle is no longer in the search results. Search again.
col.name: Name
otherHint: Not a book format KOReader opens
err.notLinked: The Kindle is not linked right now.
err.outsideLibrary: That path is outside the library.
newFolder.placeholder: New folder name, Enter to create
meta.dir: KOReader keeps reading progress in its own folder (metadata mode "dir"). ember will not move or rename books here: their progress would stay behind.
meta.hash: KOReader finds reading progress by file content (metadata mode "hash"), so it follows moved and renamed books.
warn.sidecar_shared: {path} shares its progress folder with another book, so that stayed in place
warn.sidecar_left: {path} is gone but its progress folder could not be removed
dlg.deleteBody: {what} will be removed from the Kindle:
dlg.progressLost: Reading progress and highlights of these books will be lost with them.
dlg.openDelete: KOReader has one of these books open right now. Close it on the Kindle first: otherwise KOReader may write its progress back after the book is gone.
dlg.openMove: KOReader has this book open right now. If it moves or is renamed, KOReader writes the reading progress back to the old place when it closes the book, and the book loses it. Close the book on the Kindle first, or go ahead anyway.
err.collision: That name is already taken there (the Kindle ignores upper and lower case):
err.metadataMode: KOReader's metadata mode keeps reading progress somewhere a move or rename would leave it behind. To organize books with ember, set Settings → Document → Book metadata location to "doc" in KOReader.
err.intoItself: A folder cannot go inside itself.
err.libraryRoot: The library root itself cannot be changed.
err.extensionChange: A book keeps its format, so keep its extension:
err.partial: The change failed halfway and could not be undone:
err.badRequest: ember sent a request the server refused:
err.name.encoding: The name is not valid text.
err.name.control: Names cannot contain control characters such as tabs or line breaks.
err.name.trailing: Names cannot end with a dot or a space.
err.name.too_long: The name is longer than 240 bytes.
err.name.hidden: Names cannot start with a dot: the Kindle would hide them.
err.name.sidecar: Names ending in .sdr belong to KOReader's reading progress.
err.noSpace: Not enough free space on the Kindle.
err.incomplete: The upload stopped before the whole file arrived.
err.notFile: That is a folder, not a file:
warn.replaced_left: the old file could not be deleted and is still there as {path}
queue.title: Uploads
up.notBookHint: KOReader does not open this format; it is uploaded anyway
up.noSpace: Does not fit: {size} to send, {free} free on the Kindle
up.folderThere: A folder named {name} is already there
up.lost: The connection to ember broke off during the upload
dlg.replaceKeeps: Replacing writes the new file under the same name, so KOReader keeps the reading progress and highlights it has for it. The old file is deleted.
dlg.replaceOpen: KOReader has this book open right now. Close it on the Kindle first: until then it keeps reading the old file.
pwd.banner: Anyone on your network gets root on your Kindle while its SSH server runs.
set.title: Settings
set.rootHint: A folder inside /mnt/us. Checked on the Kindle when you save, so the Kindle must be linked.
set.portHint: 2222 for KOReader's SSH server, 22 for usbnetlite.
set.awakeOn: Keep the Kindle awake while linked
set.awakeHint: A sleeping Kindle drops Wi-Fi. ember stops its screen saver while linked and lets it sleep again when you close the tab or quit ember.
set.languageHint: Applies at once and is remembered by this browser.
set.err.rootMissing: That folder does not exist on the Kindle.
set.err.rootNotFolder: That is a file on the Kindle, not a folder.
set.err.rootNeedsLink: The Kindle must be linked to check a new library root.
pwd.title: Passwordless mode
pwd.about: For when KOReader's "Login without password" stays on: ember logs in without its key. The Kindle's host key is still checked on every connection.
pwd.dlgBody: ember will log in to your Kindle without its key, through KOReader's "Login without password". It still refuses any host that does not present your Kindle's host key.
pwd.dlgKindle: Leave "Login without password (DANGEROUS)" ticked in KOReader's SSH server settings for this to work.
pwd.dlgWarn: Anyone on your network gets root on your Kindle while its SSH server runs. They can read, change or delete anything on it.
forget.title: Forget this Kindle
forget.about: Deletes the pairing: the address, the pinned host key and ember's key pair. You then pair this Kindle, or another one, from the start.
forget.dlgBody: ember deletes the pairing and its own key pair from this computer, then goes back to pairing. Nothing on the Kindle changes.
forget.dlgKey: ember's old public key stays in koreader/settings/SSH/authorized_keys on the Kindle, but it opens nothing any more: its private half is gone. You may delete that line.
err.rootOutside: The library root must be a folder inside /mnt/us.
err.badPort: The port must be a number from 1 to 65535.
err.badUser: The user must be a plain name such as root.
err.confirmationRequired: The confirmation expired or was already used. Try again.
log.pwdOff: Passwordless mode is off. ember logs in with its key again.
log.forgotten: Kindle forgotten. Pair a Kindle to continue.
err.addressNotLocal: Only addresses on this computer's local network are accepted: private (such as 192.168.x.x or 10.x.x.x), link-local or loopback.
err.keyWaitTimeout: ember stopped waiting: a key-only login never worked. Check that the key is in koreader/settings/SSH/authorized_keys and that KOReader's SSH server runs with "Login with key only", then pick your Kindle again.
err.serverDown: ember is not answering. Is it still running?
err.copy: Could not copy. Select the key and copy it by hand.
err.name.invalid: That name cannot be used on the Kindle.
pair.candidateError: ember could not read this host. Hover for details.
pair.awaitingBody: Add the key below to koreader/settings/SSH/authorized_keys over USB, then start KOReader's SSH server with "Login with key only". ember keeps trying and moves on by itself once the key works.
meta.unknown: KOReader uses a metadata mode ember does not know ("{mode}"). ember will not move or rename books here: their progress could stay behind.
rename.label: New name for {name}
newFolder.label: New folder name
log.movePartial: Move to {to} stopped at {failed}. Moved: {moved}. Everything else stayed where it was.
dlg.uploadsRoot: Uploads still in the queue were meant for the current library root. Changing it cancels them, including the file being sent now.
dlg.uploadsForget: Uploads still in the queue are cancelled, including the file being sent now.
set.uploadsKept: Not saved: the uploads keep going.
clean.title: Clean names · {where}
clean.reading: Reading the titles and authors inside the books…
clean.none: Every book name here is already clean.
clean.keeps: Reading progress and highlights go with each book. Edit a clean name before renaming if you like.
clean.pick: Pick at least one name to rename.
src.metadataHint: Title and author read from inside the book
src.patternHint: Taken apart from a download site's naming
src.genericHint: Noise stripped from the file name
log.cleanPartial: Cleaning names in {to} stopped at {failed}. Renamed: {renamed}. The rest kept their names.
set.cleanUploadsHint: Books land as "Title - Author.ext", worked out from the file name. Turn off to keep each file's own name.
theme.autoHint: The theme follows your system. Click for light.
theme.darkHint: Dark theme. Click to follow your system again.
disc.title: Disconnect from the Kindle?
disc.body: ember closes the link and stops looking for the Kindle until you click Search again.
disc.stopAbout: Turning the SSH server off does what KOReader's menu does (Settings → Network → SSH server → Stop): the Kindle stops accepting connections until you start it again. It is the safer choice, since a server left on stays reachable from your network.
disc.stop: Disconnect and turn off the Kindle's SSH server (recommended)
log.disconnected: Disconnected. Click Search again to reconnect.
log.disconnectedStopped: Disconnected. The Kindle's SSH server is turning off; start it again in KOReader to reconnect.
err.stopFailed: Disconnected, but the Kindle's SSH server may still be on. Turn it off in KOReader: Settings → Network → SSH server.
